newsitem.title: FRANCE: French CPI drop due to seasonal factors - govt.
newsitem.headline: French CPI drop due to seasonal factors - govt.

text.p: The drop in French August consumer prices reported earlier was due to seasonal factors in a month that traditionally shows subdued price pressure, the finance ministry said on Friday.
National statistics institute INSEE said on Friday that consumer prices fell 0.2-0.3 percent in August after falling 0.2 percent in July.
"Because of seasonal factors, the month of August is traditionally a month of price stability," the ministry said in a statement.
"These seasonal factors are much more pronounced this year since the price of fresh produce fell 9.7 percent. Without fresh produce prices, the index rose 0.1 percent."

The ministry said that fresh produce prices fell 5.5 percent in August 1994 and 1995. The overall index was stable in August in 1993 and 1994 and its rise in August 1995 was due to the increase in the value added tax (sales tax) that month, it said.
The ministry statement also said the 1.1 percent drop in public service prices was due to the cut in France Telecom tariffs on July 9 and 13.
The government said it expected the drop to 1.6-1.7 percent in year-on-year inflation would be confirmed in the months ahead as last year's increase in VAT was absorbed.
